A CRM requirements checklist is a structured inventory of the critical functions, workflows, data fields, user roles, and reporting needs your business expects from a CRM system. It typically categorizes requirements into must-haves, nice-to-haves, and future considerations, providing clarity when evaluating different software options. Creating this checklist before comparing vendors ensures you're matching features against actual operational needs rather than being swayed by marketing claims. Which core CRM features are essential for most businesses? Most organizations require contact and account management, pipeline or opportunity tracking, activity logging, basic automation (like task reminders), and robust reporting features. Access controls, email integration, and customizable fields are also common essentials to ensure proper data handling and user collaboration. While some industries need specialized functions, these foundational features form the backbone of effective CRM for a wide range of teams. How can I avoid hidden CRM costs? Preventing hidden CRM costs starts with a careful review of pricing models, such as per-seat licensing, upgrade tiers, and mandatory add-ons. Many generic CRM systems look affordable initially but accumulate expenses through user-based fees and extra modules. Solutions like Miniloop take a different approach by eliminating per-seat charges and letting businesses pay only for truly needed features, which can significantly reduce long-term CRM expenses for larger teams. When is a custom CRM solution a better choice than off-the-shelf? A custom CRM makes sense when your workflows are highly specialized or you require infrastructure independence and strict data ownership. Off-the-shelf tools often force process adaptations or expensive workarounds, leading to inefficiencies and increased costs. For organizations with complex requirements or high CRM expenditures, like Miniloop's ideal customers, a tailored solution aligns technology closely with business processes and can offer major cost efficiencies over time. What happens if my CRM requirements are poorly defined? If requirements are vague or incomplete, you risk choosing a CRM that either overwhelms users with unnecessary features or lacks vital capabilities. The consequences can include redundant workflows, low adoption, data silos, and costly customizations after implementation. Poorly specified requirements often translate into both operational inefficiency and higher total cost of ownership. How do I ensure my CRM integrates with existing business tools? Start by listing all critical systems, like email, ERP, marketing automation, and support tools, that require data exchange with your CRM. During the requirements phase, specify which data flows are essential and whether pre-built connectors or APIs are needed. Assessing vendor compatibility early prevents integration headaches later and supports smoother workflows across business functions. How should I prioritize CRM requirements for my organization? Rank your requirements by operational impact: must-haves are those needed for day-to-day processes, while nice-to-haves might boost efficiency but are not mission-critical. Involve stakeholders from each department to validate what is truly essential, using your process map as a reference point. Clear prioritization steers vendor selection and implementation, ensuring you invest in features that deliver the highest value. What roles should participate in defining CRM requirements? Input should come from all users who interact with customer data, including frontline sales, marketing, support teams, and their managers. IT should be involved to address integration and security considerations, while leadership can clarify strategic needs and budget constraints. Broad participation ensures the selected CRM meets real-world requirements across the business. What’s the difference between CRM features I need now vs. future needs? Features necessary right now directly support existing workflows and data requirements, while future needs might relate to planned growth, additional sales functions, or expansions into new markets. When selecting a CRM, prioritize critical current needs but leave room for the system to adapt as your business evolves. Overestimating future needs can result in wasted spend on unused features, so strike a balance based on reasonable projections. How can I migrate data safely to a new CRM system? A safe migration involves careful planning: start by auditing your current data, cleaning and standardizing records, and mapping fields between old and new systems. Always test the migration process using a sample dataset before moving everything. For teams migrating from legacy systems, custom CRM providers like Miniloop offer full data migration as part of their tailored implementation process, reducing risk and supporting data integrity.

Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Continued Growth in Same Store Revenue, Gross Profit and Unit Volume in the Second Quarter CHANDLER, Ariz. , Aug. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — RideNow Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: RDNW), (“we”, “our”, the “Company”, or “RideNow”), today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Key Second Quarter 2026 Highlights (Compared to Second Quarter 2025) Total revenue decreased 1.0%, primarily due to our store consolidation effort coupled with our former transportation services which ceased operations at the end of December 2025. On a same store sales basis, Powersports Revenue was up 3.0%, driven by a 1.7% increase in unit sales. Total gross profit was $84.8 million, up 1.1% as compared to $83.9 million. Selling, general & administrative expenses (“SG&A”) were $65.0 million, or 76.7% of gross profit, compared to $66.7 million, or 79.5% of gross profit. Net income improved to $6.5 million as compared to a net loss of $32.2 million in the prior year, which included a franchise right impairment charge of $34.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $20.5 million from $17.2 million, up 19.2%. Commenting on the quarter, Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and President Michael Quartieri said, “I am incredibly proud of our team’s execution and the substantial progress we have made on our “back to our roots” strategy. title: Interactive Videos for Online Stores: Types, Tips, and Tools
summary: Depending on the format you choose, interactive videos can encourage sales, educate audiences, or create deep engagement opportunities.
body_text: Interactive videos let consumers engage with video content directly. Viewers can respond to questions, access additional context, or explore products without ever leaving the video. Publishing these videos lets you engage with potential customers in a format they like. According to the 2025 State of Video Technology Report from Idomoo, 77% of consumers say they’re interested in interactive content from brands. Gen Z and millennials are particularly likely to want this content, according to the report. Ahead, learn more about different types of interactive videos, and discover tools for making interactive video content yourself. What are interactive videos? Interactive videos invite viewers to engage directly, allowing them to click on interactive features such as product previews and quizzes. These features can provide additional information, introduce a shopping opportunity, or give viewers the option to change the course of the video. To make interactive videos, creators start with standard video footage. They then use a specialized platform such as Vimeo or HP5 and incorporate clickable elements into the editing process via new data layers. Create must-share videos Use this free video briefing template to plan TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube video ads that will attract maximum clicks. Download template Types of interactive videos Shoppable videos Branching logic or choose-your-own-path videos Quizzes and polls Informational videos Depending on the format you choose, interactive videos can encourage sales, educate audiences, or create deep engagement opportunities. Here are the most common types to explore: Shoppable videos Shoppable videos include embedded product links. Viewers can click on featured items, review basic information, and add products to their shopping cart without leaving the video. This experience streamlines the shopping experience by allowing viewers to take action as soon as a product in the video sparks their interest. Branching logic or choose-your-own-path videos Branching logic videos create a personalized viewing experience. Interactive elements appear at specific points in the video. They provide several options and ask the viewer to choose how they’d like to continue. After making a selection, viewers see video clips or informational blurbs tailored to their response. Potential use cases for ecommerce businesses include providing tailored product recommendations or walking consumers through an onboarding process . Quizzes and polls Businesses use polls and surveys to collect customer data, often in the form of multiple-choice questions. Interactive quiz videos use multiple-choice or fill-in-the-blank questions to test the viewer’s knowledge. Quizzes appear at pre-specified points in the videos, with questions typically related to that portion of the video. Similar to branching logic videos, viewers may see a custom message, such as an explanation of the correct answer, after they input their response. This format is a popular choice for employee training videos and other educational materials. Interspersing learning material with quizzes can help keep learners engaged , according to a study in the scientific journal Cognitive Research: Principles and Implications. Another study in the same journal found that quizzes can improve information retention . Informational videos Interactive informational videos use clickable elements to add additional context to specific points in a video. Editors may choose to add interactive opportunities to entire frames or to elements within a frame. In a product demonstration video, for example, clickable pop-ups could appear over a key feature or during a specific step to expand out information for those who need it or keep it minimized for those who don’t. Tools to create interactive videos Vimeo Firework Eko HP5 Social media platforms The best interactive video platform for you depends on your budget and the type of content you want to create: Vimeo Vimeo ’s video creation tool has a drag-and-drop interface for editing without extensive experience. The editor includes preset options for adding multiple-choice questions, branching paths, and shoppable elements. Creators upload their base footage and decide how to display videos. Plans include access to Vimeo’s Shopify-compatible media player. Once you upload them to the platform, you can display your videos anywhere on your ecommerce website. Pricing: Vimeo offers three standard pricing packages, ranging from $12 to $75 per month, with enterprise pricing upon request. The basic tier includes one user profile. Firework Firework is an ecommerce-focused video platform that helps business owners turn short-form social videos into shoppable content and embed videos on their websites. Firework syncs with social media platforms like TikTok and YouTube so that you can import user-generated content (UGC) and add clickable elements to existing videos. Interactive options include shoppable videos, polls, and multiple-choice quiz questions. Firework offers multiple layouts, such as video galleries and grids, for featuring videos on your website. Templates are optimized for display on both mobile and desktop devices. This platform also supports shoppable livestreaming. It’s fully Shopify compatible, and videos can sync to the Shop app for product discovery. Firework also includes AI features such as video generation and an AI assistant. Pricing: Firework offers small business and enterprise pricing tiers. Contact a representative for pricing details. Eko Eko specializes in product videos. The program turns static images into videos that AI tools can parse. Plans provide access to Eko’s AI-powered content creation studio, which lets creators make video assets like product walk-throughs and asset management tools for adding interactive elements to Eko-created or imported video footage. Eko supports branching and informational interactive content and is fully Shopify compatible. Pricing: Eko offers custom pricing plans. Connect with a representative for information. H5P H5P is a free, open-source tool for creating interactive content directly in your browser. This platform lets creators add interactive elements on top of videos. It supports multiple-choice questions, fill-in-the-blank questions, branching logic questions, links, and more. H5P is easy to use, making it a good option for educators looking to add interactive content to learning materials. Pricing: Free Social media platforms YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram let creators and businesses add clickable tag products to videos. Viewers click these tags to start a shopping journey. Shopify has integrations with these social media sites. These integrations allow business owners to create shoppable content and sync their catalogs for in-app shopping, among other features. For example, the YouTube Shopping integration lets business owners tag products in videos and set up an in-app store that allows shoppers to buy products without leaving YouTube. Some content formats, like Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, also allow users to make videos interactive through stickers. Interactive stickers include polls and questions with spaces for viewers to write in answers. Pricing: Free Work smarter with apps Expand your store features with more than 8,000 apps from the Shopify App Store. Find everything from dropshipping suppliers to AI-powered customer support and additional apps to help you do more. Browse apps Tips for creating your own interactive videos The best interactive videos are engaging, user-friendly, and genuinely useful. Focusing on the viewer’s experience and what you hope to achieve can help your team create the most impactful content. Keep these considerations in mind: Establish goals for your content. Whether your goal is sales or employee training, prioritize adding elements that support the main goal. Trying to achieve too many things with one video could overwhelm the viewer. Consider the viewer’s POV. Ask yourself what your target audience might need and consider how you can use interactive elements to guide them through their customer journey . If they’re at the beginning of their journey, for example, use interactive pop-ups to tell your brand story in an engaging way. Post-purchase, use interactive tools to gather feedback and reviews. Offer meaningful interactions. Use interactive elements sparingly, and focus on adding real value. Adding a feature to every frame could make your video feel distracting or overwhelming. Identify moments in your video where viewers might have questions or may benefit from additional information. Guide viewers through interactive elements. Highlight interactive elements with visual cues or short on-screen prompts. Simple markers like bullet points help viewers understand that they can click directly on the screen. Consider providing brief instructions to explain how to interact with quiz or branching logic videos. Interactive videos FAQ How do interactive videos work? Interactive videos use clickable elements like product links, fill-in-the-blank questions, or multiple choice questions to turn passive viewers into active participants. They allow viewers to engage directly with video content as it plays. Are interactive videos effective for ecommerce? Interactive videos can provide consumer education, cultivate engagement, and encourage viewers to take the next step in your desired customer journey. Including interactive elements like product links or lead capture forms can help keep viewers moving through the sales funnel . Can interactive videos increase conversions? Interactivevideo is still a relatively new format. A 2025 market report conducted by videomarketingcompany Idomoo suggests that consumers are 58% more likely to buy from brands that use advanced video technology, such as interactive video content.

title: Prepaid Expense Schedule Template: A Ready-to-Use Framework for Small Teams
summary: Explore our prepaid expense schedule template designed for small teams. Ensure clarity and compliance in your financial reviews. Get started now!
body_text: Your prepaid rollforward can tie to the GL and still fail review. A spreadsheet can carry the formula, but the reviewer still needs to see which invoice supports the balance and why amortization starts in that period. Prior workpapers and review conventions supply that logic. A prepaid expense schedule template is useful only when it preserves those decisions instead of forcing the team to rebuild them at every close. A prepaid expense schedule template is useful only when it carries the source, calculation, accounting treatment, exceptions, and reviewer sign-off together. The spreadsheet itself isn’t the control. The control is whether another accountant can trace each balance, understand the treatment, and approve the entry without rebuilding the schedule. Key Takeaways: Build the prepaid schedule around reviewer questions, not just the rollforward formula. Retain invoices, contracts, service dates, and approval evidence at the line level. Separate accounting policy from schedule mechanics so neither gets buried in spreadsheet formulas. Reconcile beginning balance, additions, expense recognition, and ending balance before drafting the journal entry. Route missing support, changed terms, and unusual balances to the reviewer instead of forcing the schedule to clear. Keep Sage Intacct or QuickBooks Online as the system of record after the prepared schedule is approved. Why Prepaid Expense Schedule Templates Fail at Review Prepaid expense schedule templates fail when they prove the ending balance without proving how each line got there. A formula can calculate monthly expense correctly while carrying the wrong service period, account mapping, entity, or cutoff. Review begins at the source document, not at the total row. A Tied Schedule Can Still Be Incomplete At 4:40 PM on close day, a staff accountant drops a $24,000 annual software invoice into the prepaid rollforward. The workbook divides the amount across twelve months, updates the current-month expense, and ties the ending prepaid balance to the GL to the penny. Then the controller asks one question during review: where did the service start date come from? The invoice shows only a billing date, and the governing contract is sitting unread in someone else’s inbox. The number is right. The support isn’t there. Nothing in that scene means the preparer did poor work. The prepaid expense schedule template simply asked for less evidence than the reviewer needed. A schedule can foot, cross-foot, and tie while still leaving the accounting treatment unsupported. Before approving a template, check whether each line answers five questions: What source document supports the asset? Which dates define the eligible service period? Which account, department, entity, or other dimension applies? What changed from the prior period? Who reviewed the treatment and the resulting journal entry? A missing answer shouldn’t disappear inside a formula. It belongs in the exception queue. Generic Formulas Hide Team-Specific Treatment Two accounting teams can receive the same annual software invoice and prepare different schedules without either team making a mistake. One may begin recognition on the contract start date. Another may follow a documented convention for partial periods. Their account mappings, dimensional coding, capitalization rules, and review thresholds may differ as well. That variation is why a generic prepaid schedule template rarely survives unchanged. The formulas are reusable. The accounting logic isn’t. A useful template makes the team’s treatment visible in dedicated fields or reviewer notes instead of relying on a preparer to remember how the prior workbook was built. Spreadsheets have real strengths here. They’re flexible, familiar, and easy to adjust when a contract changes, which is a fair reason to keep them for a small, stable population of prepaids. The risk appears when that flexibility hardens into undocumented logic spread across tabs, hidden cells, and prior-period copies, where the next reviewer has no way to see the decision that produced the number. If you want to inspect how source documents, schedule logic, and reviewer actions stay together, See Truewind in action . The Review Surface Matters More Than the Layout Think of a prepaid schedule as a bridge workpaper between the source document and the GL. If the bridge only shows the ending balance, the reviewer still has to climb down into invoices, contracts, emails, and prior files to confirm that it holds. A polished layout doesn’t reduce that climb. Review-ready means the accountant can move in both directions. Starting with the schedule, the reviewer can reach the invoice and treatment. Starting with the GL balance, the reviewer can reach the supporting lines, current-period expense, proposed journal entry, and approval record. Controllers aren’t primarily worried about a spreadsheet that is obviously broken. They’re worried about a clean schedule whose logic can’t be traced. The better question is not whether the prepaid expense schedule template works. It is whether the reviewer can prove why it works. How to Build a Review-Ready Prepaid Expense Schedule Build a review-ready prepaid expense schedule by connecting every rollforward line to its source, treatment, calculation, exception status, and approval. Keep policy choices visible and formulas repeatable. The schedule should prepare the journal entry while giving the reviewer enough evidence to confirm it. Diagnose the Gaps Before Rebuilding the Template Start with the review path, not the column order. Open the last approved prepaid schedule and select a line that required a correction or follow-up, then trace it from the source document through the schedule, journal entry, and reviewer note. Wherever the trail breaks, the template is relying on memory or off-workpaper evidence. Four questions expose most structural gaps. Can the reviewer find the source without searching email? Can they see why recognition began in that period? Can they identify which rule or prior treatment informed the coding? Can they tell what the preparer changed after review? A single “no” points to a missing control surface, not merely a missing spreadsheet field. If two or more come back “no” on the same line, the workbook isn’t your problem; the process behind it is. Run the diagnostic on these parts of the workflow: Source completeness: Confirm that every addition has an invoice, contract, or other approved support. Treatment visibility: Record the service period, account mapping, dimensions, and relevant policy choice. Calculation traceability: Show how the current-period expense and remaining balance were calculated. Exception handling: Separate unresolved items from ordinary schedule lines. Approval evidence: Retain who reviewed the schedule and what changed before approval. A new workbook won’t fix a process that still stores treatment in someone’s head. Fix the trail first. Build a Source Register Before the Rollforward The source register should establish what entered the prepaid workflow before any amortization formula runs. For each addition, record the vendor, document identifier, invoice date, covered service period, amount, entity, and location of the supporting document. The goal is simple: no schedule line without a named source. Completeness matters as much as extraction. An invoice may reference an agreement that defines the actual service dates. A renewal may replace a prior contract mid-period. Credit activity may change the asset after the original invoice was scheduled. If the source packet is incomplete, the line should stay visible as an exception rather than entering the prepaid expense schedule with an assumed answer. A practical intake sequence looks like this: Collect current-period invoices, contracts, credits, and amendments. Match each document to an existing prepaid line or identify it as a new addition. Compare the source packet with the prior-period schedule and relevant GL activity. Flag missing service dates, unclear entities, or changed terms. Release complete items into schedule preparation and route the rest for review. Stopping incomplete items at intake feels slower, and it is, on that one line, on that one day. In practice, the work already exists. The difference is whether it happens once in a visible queue or three times over: once during preparation, again during review, and a third time when audit support asks the same question six months later. Give Every Line Enough Accounting Context A useful prepaid expense schedule template treats each line as a small workpaper. The amount and monthly expense aren’t enough. The reviewer also needs to see what the asset represents, which period receives the expense, where the entry will post, and whether the treatment follows an established rule. Keep the line-level structure readable. Dense workbooks often combine source details, formulas, policy choices, and review notes in the same cells because that layout grew over several closes. Pulling those elements apart makes the schedule easier to inspect without removing flexibility. At minimum, each line should carry: Source fields: Vendor, document identifier, invoice date, support location Treatment fields: Service start, service end, recognition convention, account Dimension fields: Entity, department, location, fund, program, or other required coding Calculation fields: Original amount, additions, expense recognized, remaining balance Review fields: Exception status, preparer note, reviewer action, approval status To test that line-level structure against a schedule your team already owns, Book a Truewind demo . Separate Policy Decisions From Schedule Math The schedule should calculate an approved treatment, not decide the treatment for you. Recognition timing, partial-period conventions, capitalization rules, and account selection belong to the accounting team. Once those choices are documented, the workbook can apply them consistently. A basic formula may divide the capitalized amount across eligible periods, but the formula can’t establish whether those periods are correct. That answer comes from the source documents and the team’s policy. If contract terms change or a credit appears, the line needs review before the revised calculation flows into the journal entry. Keep three layers distinct: Policy: The rule the accounting team has approved. Treatment: How that rule applies to the specific source document. Calculation: The formula that carries the treatment through the schedule. Some teams prefer formulas that handle every possible edge case, and the appeal is understandable: one workbook, no exceptions to chase. Yet a formula that tries to settle ambiguous service dates or changed contract terms hides judgment inside workbook logic, exactly where the reviewer has the least visibility. Here is a rule of thumb worth keeping: if resolving a line requires reading the contract rather than reading the cell, it is an exception, not a formula input. Let formulas handle repeatable math and let accountants handle exceptions. Reconcile the Rollforward to the GL The prepaid rollforward should explain the full movement from the prior closing balance to the current closing balance. Beginning balance, additions, current-period expense, credits, disposals, and other adjustments need to connect without plugs. Any unexplained difference remains an exception until the reviewer resolves it. Start with the last approved schedule, not an unreviewed working copy. Confirm that its ending balance equals the current schedule’s beginning balance. Then compare additions with source documents and GL activity, recalculate expense recognition, and tie the ending schedule to the prepaid GL account. The reviewer should be able to follow this sequence: Prior approved ending balance becomes the current beginning balance. Supported additions and approved adjustments enter the rollforward. Current-period expense is calculated from visible service periods and treatment. The ending schedule is compared with the GL balance. The proposed journal entry explains the difference that should be posted. No plug should be labeled “true-up” without an explanation. A true-up may be valid, but the schedule still needs to show which source, changed assumption, or prior error produced it. Design the Journal Entry and Review Together A prepaid schedule shouldn’t end with a total that someone rekeys into the ERP. It should prepare the journal-entry draft with the same accounts, dimensions, descriptions, and source references the reviewer just inspected. Re-entry creates another place for coding and amount differences to appear. The review flow should separate prepared work from judgment items. Ordinary lines that follow approved treatment can move through a standard review. Missing support, changed terms, unusual balance movements, and new policy questions should remain visible until an accountant decides what happens next. Your team only reviews the exceptions in depth, while retaining sign-off over the full schedule and entry. A final review should confirm: The schedule begins with the last approved ending balance. Each current-period addition has complete source support. Service periods and coding follow approved treatment. Exceptions have documented reviewer decisions. The schedule ties to the GL after the proposed entry. Nothing posts before reviewer approval. The reviewer isn’t a final checkbox. The reviewer owns the accounting result. How Truewind Prepares Review-Ready Prepaid Schedules Truewind prepares prepaid schedules upstream of Sage Intacct and QuickBooks Online, which remain the systems of record. It combines prior workpapers, current-period source documents, and ERP balances into a review surface where accountants can inspect treatment, correct exceptions, and approve the output before anything moves downstream. Source-Linked Schedule Preparation and Rollforward Truewind’s prepaid and fixed asset schedule capability ingests source documents and the prior-period schedule, rolls balances forward, and prepares current-period support using the team’s existing treatment. Workpaper generation retains the link between each schedule line, its source, its calculation, and any journal-entry draft. It doesn’t invent accounting policy or resolve unclear treatment without the reviewer. Historical-example learning carries confirmed treatment and reviewer corrections into later periods. That matters because recurring accounting work isn’t generic. A prepaid expense schedule template for one team may use different account mappings, dimensions, cutoffs, and recognition conventions from another team, even when the source document looks similar. One accounting firm described the capacity effect plainly: “Truewind automates a huge chunk of that busywork.” The same customer conversation went further: “It's not just about making bookkeeping simpler; it's about freeing up teams, and helping them focus on higher-value projects.” Those statements describe one customer’s experience, not a promised result for every accounting team. Accountant Review Before the General Ledger Truewind presents prepared schedules, journal-entry drafts, source links, and exceptions in a human review workflow. Accountants can confirm the work, adjust it, or return an item for further preparation. The audit trail retains the sources, coding decisions, corrections, and reviewer actions associated with the workflow. Approved output can then move to Sage Intacct or QuickBooks Online with coding and dimensions preserved. Keep Sage or QBO as your source of truth. Truewind doesn’t replace the ledger, post without reviewer confirmation, or settle exceptions on its own. A customer discussing recurring categorization said, “Categorization is accurate, and we stopped having to double-check everything.” Another customer opened with, “Truewind has been amazing.” Both are customer-specific observations. The mechanism underneath them is the part that matters here: preparation follows captured rules, exceptions stay visible, and the accountant approves the result. If that review path matches the controls your close already requires, Get a Truewind demo . What a Strong Prepaid Workflow Preserves A strong prepaid workflow preserves more than the ending balance. It keeps the source document, service period, accounting treatment, calculation, exceptions, journal-entry draft, and reviewer decision connected. That is what turns a prepaid expense schedule template from a recurring spreadsheet into a reviewable accounting process. Automation belongs in the preparation work between source files and the GL. Judgment stays with the accountant. To manage edge cases in your prepaid expense schedule, start by clearly documenting any exceptions. 1) Identify the specific situation that deviates from your standard process. 2) Use Truewind to capture these exceptions and ensure they are visible for review. This way, your team can address them without losing track of the overall workflow. 3) Always route these items to the appropriate reviewer for judgment before finalizing any entries. When should I review my prepaid expense schedules? You should review your prepaid expense schedules regularly, ideally before each close. 1) Schedule a review session after preparing the initial draft of your prepaid schedule. 2) Use Truewind’s human-in-the-loop review workflow to ensure that all entries are checked against source documents and accounting policies. 3) This proactive approach helps catch any discrepancies early, making the final approval process smoother and more reliable. Why does my prepaid expense schedule need a source register? A source register is crucial for maintaining clarity and accuracy in your prepaid expense schedules. 1) It tracks every entry back to its original source, such as invoices or contracts, ensuring that you have the necessary documentation for review. 2) Truewind can help you create this register, which makes it easier to manage and verify entries. 3) This practice enhances your audit trail and supports compliance during reviews.

title: Channels
summary: Learn how bank99 partnered with Diebold Nixdorf to deliver ATM-as-a-Service solution in just three months.
body_text: bank99 is a truly Austrian brand, committed to the local communities it serves and passionate about innovating for the future of banking. From its inception, it’s a financial institution that’s moved quickly and decisively—it launched in April, 2020, just 337 days after the project was kicked off, with the goal of serving 99% of Austrian consumers. A joint venture between Austrian Post AG and the GRAWE Banking Group, it offers financial services to Austrian Post customers. bank99 opted for Diebold Nixdorf’s subscription model to deploy a self-service channel aimed at offering advanced transaction sets while driving efficiencies and optimizing their entire self-service network. title: Thermal Imaging Mining Systems: Conveyors and Kilns
summary: Thermal imaging mining systems watch conveyors, kilns, and heavy equipment so failures surface early. What OEMs should know before specifying one.
body_text: Mining and heavy industry give thermal camera systems the hardest job in the industrial world, and the platforms that win are the ones designed around that reality from the start. Conveyors, kilns, and mobile fleets each generate predictable heat signatures, and deviations from those signatures are the earliest reliable warning of failure. Dust, vibration, moisture, and round-the-clock duty cycles wash out systems that were designed for a clean plant floor. Predictive programs built on continuous monitoring can cut facility downtime by 5 to 15 percent compared with preventive schedules alone. Optics quality, environmental sealing, and supply chain stability matter more to long-term program economics than headline sensor specs. If you are building a monitoring platform for mine sites, specify the imaging chain for the worst hour of the worst shift rather than the demo. Few environments punish equipment the way a working mine does. Crushers run at capacity, conveyors stretch for kilometers, haul trucks cycle around the clock, and everything operates inside a permanent cloud of abrasive dust. When something overheats out there, the cost of finding out late is measured in lost production hours rather than repair invoices. That is why thermal imaging mining applications have moved from occasional inspection routes to permanently installed monitoring. The economics are straightforward. Deloitte's analysis of predictive maintenance programs points to a 5 to 15 percent reduction in facility downtime when condition-based monitoring replaces calendar-driven servicing, along with 70 to 75 percent fewer breakdowns versus a reactive approach. Applied to a processing plant or a haulage circuit, those percentages get large fast. For the OEMs, system integrators, and platform builders serving this market, the interesting question is not whether infrared belongs in mining. It is what a camera system has to survive to be worth installing. This piece walks through the applications that drive demand, the environmental realities that separate durable infrared imaging solutions from disappointing ones, and the criteria worth applying before you commit a design. Why Does Mining Punish Thermal Imaging Systems So Hard? Most industrial imaging specs are written against a factory baseline: controlled temperature, filtered air, a technician nearby. Mine sites offer none of that. Understanding the specific stressors helps explain why thermal imaging deployments in mining fail for reasons that have nothing to do with sensor resolution. Airborne Particulates Never Stop Ore dust, coal dust, and drill fines coat every exposed surface. Window contamination degrades apparent temperature readings before anyone notices a problem, which means calibration drift shows up as false confidence rather than an obvious fault. Purge air, sacrificial windows, and coating durability become design requirements rather than accessories. Vibration and Shock Are Continuous Crusher housings, screen decks, and haul truck frames transmit constant mechanical energy into anything bolted to them. Optical assemblies that hold alignment on a bench can wander in the field, and a misaligned lens stack quietly degrades image quality over months. Robust mounting and mechanically stable optical design carry real weight here. Service Windows Are Rare Mines operate around the clock, and a monitoring system that needs a technician every few weeks is a liability. Uncooled long wave infrared systems, operating in the 8 to 14 micrometer band, dominate mining thermal inspection work for exactly this reason: no cryocooler, low power draw, and long service intervals. Higher-temperature process work sometimes calls for mid wave systems in the 3 to 5 micrometer band, which is a separate design conversation covered in our guide to thermal cameras in harsh environments . What Do Thermal Imaging Mining Systems Actually Watch? Three asset families account for most of the demand, and each one shapes system requirements differently. A platform built for industrial thermal imaging applications across all three needs flexibility in optics, mounting, and output rather than one fixed configuration. Conveyors and Transfer Points Conveyor thermal monitoring is the most established use case in the sector. Seized idlers, misaligned belts, and slipping drive pulleys all generate friction heat well before they generate visible damage. Fixed cameras positioned at drive heads and transfer chutes give operators continuous coverage of the points most likely to fail. Conveyor thermal monitoring also catches hot material coming off a stockpile or out of a process line, which matters enormously for fire prevention. Kilns, Dryers, and High-Temperature Process Equipment Kiln thermal imaging supports refractory management in cement, lime, and mineral processing operations. Refractory lining thins gradually, and thinning shows up as elevated shell temperature long before a breakthrough. Continuous kiln thermal imaging lets plants schedule relines against measured condition rather than calendar assumptions. The same approach applies to dryers, calciners, and furnace enclosures where interior inspection is impractical during operation, and where purpose-built furnace camera modules generally outperform general-purpose hardware. Mobile Fleet and Heavy Equipment A heavy equipment thermal camera mounted on or aimed at haul trucks, loaders, and shovels watches brakes, hydraulics, wheel motors, and engine compartments. Brake and hydraulic faults in particular tend to announce themselves thermally well ahead of any operator-noticeable symptom, which is why this coverage has spread from the maintenance bay to the haul road. Some operators run fixed gate-style scanning stations that image every vehicle as it passes; others integrate cameras onto the machine itself. Either way, heavy equipment thermal camera data feeds the same maintenance workflow as the fixed assets. Asset Family Typical Thermal Signature Watched Common Deployment Conveyors and idlers Friction heat at rollers, pulleys, and bearings Fixed cameras at drive and transfer points Belt-carried material Hot ore, smoldering coal, combustible carryback Wide field of view over belt width Kilns and dryers Elevated shell temperature from refractory loss Fixed scanning along the shell Haul trucks and loaders Brake, hydraulic, and driveline heat Gate-style scanning or vehicle-mounted Electrical rooms and substations Loose connections, overloaded circuits Fixed panel monitoring or route-based How Does Conveyor Thermal Monitoring Reduce Fire Risk? Fire is the safety case that gets thermal imaging mining projects funded. Underground, the stakes are severe. NIOSH notes that fires in conveyor belt entries generate smoke and high concentrations of toxic gas that the ventilation system then distributes through the mine, and that ventilation air velocity strongly affects how well detection and suppression systems perform. Traditional detection relies on carbon monoxide sensors and smoke sensors, which respond once combustion is already underway. Thermal monitoring works earlier in the sequence, flagging the friction heat or the hot material that precedes ignition. The two approaches complement each other rather than compete, and mining thermal inspection programs that pair them get earlier warning without giving up proven detection methods. Regulatory structure reinforces this. MSHA's conveyor system standards cover slippage switches, belt maintenance, automatic fire warning devices, and belt entry ventilation across underground coal, surface, and metal and nonmetal operations. Systems that produce clean, auditable temperature records give operators evidence that supports those obligations, and that documentation value is a genuine selling point for platform builders. A note worth carrying into product literature: thermal imaging is strong in low-visibility conditions and has real limits in others, and honest performance framing earns more trust with technical buyers than absolute claims do. Five Criteria for Specifying a Mining Thermal Platform Selection conversations in this sector tend to start with resolution and end somewhere entirely different. These five criteria drive long-term program outcomes more reliably than any single spec line. Environmental rating matched to the actual installation. Ingress protection, operating temperature range, and vibration tolerance should reflect the worst position at the client site, not the average one. A system rated for a control room fails at a transfer chute. Optical durability under abrasion. Window materials and coatings take continuous particulate impact. Material selection and coating hardness determine whether accuracy holds through year three or degrades through month six. Integration into existing plant systems. Output protocols, alarm handling, and historian compatibility decide whether a monitoring system becomes part of the maintenance workflow or a screen nobody watches. Our industrial thermal camera specifications checklist breaks these requirements down further. Calibration stability over service life. Industrial thermal monitoring only produces value when temperature readings stay trustworthy. Ask how accuracy is maintained, how often recalibration is required, and what happens to readings as windows accumulate contamination. Supply chain depth behind the components. Mining platforms carry long service lives and long spare parts obligations. Optical material availability, particularly for germanium and its alternatives, has real program risk attached to it. Programs that plan for this early avoid redesign later. Those criteria apply differently depending on how the system gets deployed. Fixed installations for kiln thermal imaging carry different constraints than a camera bolted to a haul truck, and most mining programs end up running a mix. Deployment Model Best Suited For Main Trade-Off Fixed continuous monitoring Conveyor drives, kilns, critical electrical assets Higher install cost, highest coverage Gate or checkpoint scanning Mobile fleet passing a fixed location Snapshot data rather than continuous Vehicle-integrated cameras Machine-level health on mobile assets Tighter size, weight, and power limits Route-based portable inspection Distributed low-criticality assets Depends on inspection frequency What Should OEMs Look for in an Imaging Partner? The suppliers serving this market fall into distinct categories, and the category matters more than the brand. Component distributors offer broad catalog coverage, which works well when a standard part fits. Camera assemblers integrate purchased optics and sensors, an approach that serves many programs until a custom requirement or a supply disruption appears. Vertically integrated manufacturers control the chain from raw optical material through finished camera, which shortens development cycles and reduces the number of parties who can break your schedule. For mining programs specifically, three supplier attributes deserve weight. First, custom optical design capability, because standard focal lengths rarely match a specific conveyor geometry or kiln standoff distance. Second, domestic manufacturing and compliance positioning, which increasingly matters for infrastructure and government-adjacent projects. Third, material independence. Chalcogenide glass formulations that substitute for germanium reduce exposure to a genuinely volatile supply market, and that stability shows up in program pricing years later. Industrial thermal monitoring platforms live a long time. The imaging decisions made in the first design cycle set the ceiling on what the platform can do for the rest of its life, a theme explored further in our OEM guide to predictive maintenance imaging . Frequently Asked Questions These are the questions that come up most often in early scoping conversations with engineering and procurement teams evaluating industrial thermal monitoring for mine sites and heavy industry. Which infrared band suits mining applications best? Long wave infrared, covering 8 to 14 micrometers, handles most mining thermal inspection requirements, including conveyors, bearings, electrical assets, and general equipment monitoring. Mid wave infrared, at 3 to 5 micrometers, becomes relevant for very high-temperature process work such as kiln interiors and molten material. Match the band to the hottest and coldest assets in scope rather than defaulting to one choice. Can thermal cameras see through mine dust? Thermal imaging penetrates airborne dust, smoke, and darkness far better than visible-light cameras, which is a large part of its value underground and at transfer points. Performance still degrades in heavy rain, dense water spray, and against surfaces with strong reflected solar loading, so system design should account for those conditions. Do surface and underground operations need different systems? Underground work puts more weight on fire detection, confined-space mounting, and any applicable permissibility requirements for the mine class. Surface operations deal with wider ambient temperature swings, solar loading, and longer standoff distances across pit and stockpile areas. The core imaging requirements overlap heavily, but housings, mounting, and field of view usually diverge. Do these systems replace manual inspection routes? They shift the balance rather than eliminate inspections. Fixed monitoring covers critical assets continuously and flags anomalies between rounds, while portable inspection remains practical for distributed, lower-criticality equipment. Most mature programs run both. Build a Mining Thermal Platform That Holds Up The mine sites that get real value from infrared run systems designed for the conditions they actually face. That starts upstream of the camera housing, in the optical materials, the lens design, and the manufacturing chain behind them. LightPath Technologies designs and builds infrared optics, assemblies, and complete thermal camera systems for OEMs and integrators serving industrial and heavy industry markets, backed by proprietary Black Diamond chalcogenide glass and North American manufacturing. If you are scoping a monitoring platform for mining or heavy equipment applications, talk with our engineering team about what your program requires.

title: Evolv Alternatives: Options for Weapons Detection
summary: We review several Evolv Technology alternatives you should consider for higher education, casinos, hospitals, and more.
body_text: Security directors, hospital administrators, and campus safety leaders evaluating Evolv alternatives are often managing the same compounding problem: existing weapons detection systems create as many operational challenges as they solve. Traditional metal detectors require staff to operate at each checkpoint, generate long queues that frustrate visitors and slow facility operations, and pose a risk to individuals with implanted medical devices such as pacemakers. At the same time, many of these systems lack integrated video capture, leaving security teams without the footage they need for investigative follow-up after an incident. The stakes extend beyond hardware limitations. Accurately identifying armed individuals in no-firearm zones, without disrupting the flow of visitors, patients, or employees, remains one of the hardest problems in facility security. Add to that the pressure to keep sensitive monitoring data compliant with regulatory requirements, justify cost-per-threat ratios to leadership, and integrate new vendor infrastructure without overhauling internal processes, and the case for re-evaluating your current solution becomes difficult to ignore. What is Evolv? Evolv Technology is a weapons detection security screening company founded in 2013 in Waltham, MA. Evolv pioneered and developed a touchless security screening system that uses digital sensors and artificial intelligence to detect threats. Evolv Technology has two main solutions: Evolv Express® and Evolv eXpedite™. Evolv Express is a weapons detection system that screens individuals at an ingress point, similar to traditional metal detectors. According to Evolv, Evolv Express offers a faster, more efficient threat-screening experience than traditional metal detectors, and Evolv eXpedite works with Evolv Express to detect concealed weapons in bags using X-ray imaging and AI. What Are the Leading Evolv Technology Alternatives? While many companies and organizations have deployed Evolv Technology as part of their security solution, it may not be the best fit for every situation. In this post, we’ll introduce some Evolv alternatives and specifically dive into SoundThinking’s SafePointe state-of-the-art weapons detection technology. Further, we’ll walk through the critical features that make it a compelling Evolv alternative and standout choice for institutions prioritizing both safety and user experience. Evolv Alternative #1: SafePointe For security departments grappling with public safety challenges in high-traffic areas, the optimal solution is a concealed weapons detection system that conducts rigorous security screening without adding staff or compromising the visitor experience. Key Feature # 1: Advanced Camera, Sensors, and NVIDIA-Powered Edge Processor Precisely Assess Threat Objects SafePointe’s advanced camera combines person motion data, including velocity, position, and movements, along with magnetic moment data, to allow for the scanning of multiple entrants simultaneously. The NVIDIA®-powered edge processor captures all this data and runs it through a state-of-the-art AI model to identify an individual (or multiple individuals) carrying a firearm, enabling prompt search and resolution. Key Feature # 2: Concealed Weapons Detection System Upholds Public Safety While Blending Seamlessly into the Environment Unlike Evolv Express and traditional metal detector systems, which are highly visible and stand front and center as patrons walk in, the SafePointe concealed system is typically deployed as non-descript bollards or within approved planters to seamlessly integrate into the environment. An example of SafePointe’s nondescript bollards outside of a building. Patrons can walk into the venue freely, enjoying their experience without the looming presence of overt security measures. The discreet nature of SafePointe provides a public safety layer without sacrificing ambiance or visitor comfort. Key Feature # 3: High Throughput, Efficiently Screening Large Volumes of People Traditional metal detectors can result in long queues, frustrated visitors, and inefficient security operations. The SafePointe system, by contrast, offers high throughput and efficiently screens large volumes of people. The key to SafePointe’s efficiency is its free-flow screening technology, which ensures a touchless and seamless passage for visitors. This benefit is twofold. 1. For visitors, the experience of entering a facility becomes more pleasant. There’s no need to stop, empty pockets, or remove belts. They simply walk through, free from the usual anxieties associated with traditional security checks. 2. For security personnel, the process becomes more streamlined. SafePointe’s high throughput capacity means they can manage larger crowds more effectively, ensuring no compromise on safety. Key Feature # 4: Unmanned Screening Process That Saves Money While Upholding Rigorous Public Safety Standards SafePointe can quickly identify an individual carrying a weapon when walking through bollards alone or with others. Unlike traditional metal detectors and Evolv Express, SafePointe’s unmanned screening process stands out for its low Total Cost of Ownership (TCO). Here’s how it works: As the camera collects real-time person motion data—such as direction, speed, and movement—AI simultaneously analyzes magnetic data generated from the individual to assess whether they are carrying a weapon. If a weapon is detected, the details are forwarded to facility security in less than 10 seconds via the SafePointe app or text, including a brief video and an image of the individual. As a result of this process, SafePointe’s unmanned screening process: Enables internal security departments to appropriately respond to accurately detected threats as they arise without needing to employ additional personnel to monitor the system at each entrance. This translates directly to significant cost savings, allowing institutions to redirect these resources to other crucial areas. Supports uninterrupted coverage: Traditional manned systems, while effective during peak times with maximum staffing, can be vulnerable outside of peak hours. SafePointe’s 24/7 monitoring improves your security posture, providing institutions with additional peace of mind. Key Feature #5: Passive Sensors are Safe for Vulnerable Populations Many metal detectors and other weapons detection systems have active magnetic field-generating sensors, which can be problematic for individuals with pacemakers and other medical devices. SafePointe’s Magnetic Moment sensors are passive, making it a safe weapons detection system for these vulnerable populations. Key Feature #6: Alert with Related Video to Improve Investigative Follow-Up Unlike conventional metal detector systems that lack video capabilities, SafePointe’s system alerts the customer in less than 10 seconds, providing the image and related video. Key Feature #6: Alert Threat Levels with Related Video to Improve Investigative Follow-Up Unlike conventional metal detector systems that lack video capabilities, SafePointe’s system alerts the customer security team within six to ten seconds, providing the threat level and related video. SafePointe’s approach to security is not just about weapons detection; it’s about providing actionable intelligence in near real-time. When a potential threat is identified, the system sends a still image and video footage. The video captures the person entering the facility, allowing security personnel to assess the situation and make informed decisions about how to respond. The image and associated video footage become essential tools for any subsequent investigation, providing evidence of the event and aiding legal proceedings and reviews. In a world where every second counts during a security breach, having such detailed information can be the difference between a swift, effective response and a potentially chaotic situation. Key Feature # 7: Easy-to-Use Software with Comprehensive Reporting and Performance Metrics The InSight data platform, available via a web interface, enables the review, analysis, and sharing of SafePointe data across multiple lanes, entrances, and even different facilities and locations. The alert review summary provides details in an easy-to-read incident report to aid investigations and facilitate the sharing of safety and investigative information. The summary is available through the InSight application and can be shared internally or externally. InSight also provides daily, weekly, and monthly reporting that shows the number of visitors, alerts, and alerts published as a percentage of visitors, making it an ideal reporting tool for internal security teams to review and monitor continuously. Key Feature # 8: SOC 2 Compliance and HIPAA Compliance With SafePointe, security teams can rest assured that the sensitive data they monitor is secure and complies with regulatory requirements. As of October 2024, the SafePointe weapons detection system in the healthcare space is HIPAA compliant, and SafePointe achieved SOC 2 compliance in early 2025. Key Feature #9: Operates Separately from Your Main Network SafePointe provides ease of use from both a configuration and security perspective. Installation is available to make the deployment process hassle-free. Furthermore, the system is designed to operate independently of your security and IT networks, minimizing disruptions. Our AI system and sensors are linked to and transmit alerts via the Cloud, utilizing either a web portal interface or a smartphone application. Book a demo with our team to see what SafePointe's frictionless weapons detection would look like at your facility. Book a Demo Other Evolv Alternatives Evolv Alternative #3: Athena Security Powered by CEIA OPENGATE, the Athena Security weapons detection system comprises an HD active walkthrough metal detector and induction lidar, and includes a visual camera, artificial intelligence technologies, a controller tablet, and a monitor tablet. The system is faster than a typical airport or courthouse scanner but less sensitive, meaning it’s less likely to falsely alarm on something like a belt buckle and could be less likely to detect a weapon. Evolv Alternative #3: Opengate by Ceia CEIA is a manufacturer that designs electromagnetic metal detection equipment for security screening, offering both walk-through and handheld models. The flagship OPENGATE line is a system for screening people, backpacks, purses, and bags. CEIA serves a wide range of markets including airports, law enforcement, courts and correctional facilities, schools, event venues, and loss prevention in retail settings. Evolv Alternative #4: Xtract One Technologies Xtract One Technologies is a technology-driven threat-detection and security solution that leverages AI to provide secure patron access control experiences. Xtract One is a direct competitor to Evolv, as the two are weapons detection systems highly focused on the sporting and entertainment venue space — locations with high-volume traffic for limited periods. Checklist for Assessing Best Weapons Detection System for Your Facility Does the system provide concealed weapons detection that upholds public safety while seamlessly integrating into the environment? Does the system provide a public safety layer without sacrificing ambiance or visitor comfort? Does the system offer cost savings while upholding rigorous public safety standards? Is the system safe for individuals with medical devices, such as pacemakers? Can the system handle high traffic efficiently without causing bottlenecks? Does the system provide real-time categorized alerts with video footage for immediate and subsequent assessment? Does the system offer comprehensive reporting and performance metrics? Does the system meet all regulatory and compliance requirements? Can the system function separately from security and IT networks? Choosing the Right Weapons Detection System for Your Facility Choosing a weapons detection system is not just a procurement decision; it is a commitment to how your facility balances safety, cost, and visitor experience for years to come. Evolv Express addresses part of that equation, but for organizations weighing staffing costs, medical device safety, investigative capability, and regulatory compliance, the decision may point elsewhere. SafePointe was built to close those specific gaps: unmanned screening that lowers total cost of ownership, passive sensors that are safe for vulnerable populations, integrated video for investigative follow-up, and SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance that give security teams confidence in how their data is handled. For hospitals, healthcare facilities, corporate campuses, casinos, higher education, museums, venues, and other facilities, the right system is the one that protects people without making them feel like they're walking through a checkpoint. SafePointe's track record across high-traffic facilities reflects that balance, offering security leaders a path to stronger protection without the operational tradeoffs that come with traditional screening. title: RingCentral review: Features, pricing, pros & cons
summary: Comprehensive RingCentral review covering features, pricing, pros, cons, and who it's best for. Updated for 2026 with real user feedback.
body_text: In the market for a business phone system? If you are, then you may be considering RingCentral. Founded in 1999, RingCentral is one of the oldest cloud-based business communications platforms. It offers VoIP calling, video meetings, team events, and business SMS in one place. Its plans start at $20 per user per month. RingCentral is a solid option for mid-market and enterprise teams. For small teams, however, its feature limits and outdated interface make it hard to recommend. In this article, we conduct a thorough review of RingCentral. We’ll cover its key features, plans and pricing, and its pros and cons. We’ll highlight which teams will benefit from using RingCentral’s platform. Plus, we’ll present a RingCentral alternative that’s better suited to small and fast-growing businesses. How does RingCentral work? RingCentral uses VoIP technology to let you call and text your customers. VoIP infrastructure sends calls and texts over the internet instead of a carrier network. This enables its platform to provide calls, texts, and video calling tools on the same plan. As long as you’re connected to the internet, you can use your mobile device, laptop, or desktop computer to talk to customers and team members. Key features of RingCentral RingCentral offers everything teams need for their business communications. Here’s a list of the features RingCentral provides that make it unique: Team messaging. Collaborate with your team by sending direct messages and files to your colleagues. You can also assign follow-up tasks to your teammates. Voice calling. Unlimited domestic calling to US and Canadian numbers on all plans. Supports desk phones, softphones, and mobile apps. Video meetings. Built-in video conferencing on every plan. Supports up to 200 participants in a single meeting. Business SMS/MMS. Business texting to customers. Capped in each plan; shared texting is only available as an add-on. Multi-level auto attendant and IVR. Multi-level phone menus for routing callers. Available on all plans. Third-party integrations. 500+ integrations are available in RingCentral’s platform. You can also build your own RingCentral integrations with its API. AI features. Automatically take notes and get meeting and SMS thread summaries with RingCentral’s AI assistant. Call and video recording. RingCentral offers on-demand call recording and automatic video recording on all plans. You’ll have to upgrade to get access to automatic RingCentral call recording . Analytics. Get call log reports and quality of service dashboards on all plans. Upgrade to get even more analytics features. RingCentral pricing and plans RingCentral offers four plans. Each plan offers different features and has different limits. Here’s a look at how these plans stack up: Feature Core Advanced Ultra Customer Engagement Bundle Price per user per month $20 billed annually, $30 billed monthly $25 billed annually/$35 billed monthly $35 billed annually/$45 billed monthly Pricing isn’t public Unlimited calls to the US and Canada ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Text messaging 25 SMS/MMS per user per month 100 SMS/MMS per user per month 200 SMS/MMS per user per month 200 SMS/MMS per user per month Toll-free minutes 100 pooled 1,000 pooled 10,000 pooled 10,000 pooled Call recording On-demand Automatic and on-demand Automatic and on-demand Automatic and on-demand Here are a few things to know about RingCentral’s pricing structure: Free trial limitations. If you want to try RingCentral before you sign up for a paid plan, you can only do so with fewer than five team members. RingCentral doesn’t let you try it with larger teams. Add-ons. RingCentral has over a dozen different add-ons for teams to choose from. Some of these add-ons are for essential features like shared texting and text templates. Others are for advanced features like conversation intelligence. These add-ons can make it hard to estimate your monthly costs. Hidden fees. If you exceed your monthly usage for certain RingCentral features, you’ll be subject to overage fees. For example, if you send more than 25 SMS messages in the Core plan, every additional message costs $0.0119. You’ll find similar fees for features like toll-free minutes and additional toll-free numbers. For a full breakdown, including hidden costs and contract terms, see our RingCentral pricing guide . Pros: What RingCentral does well RingCentral offers dozens of features across its different plans. It can be confusing to know where it excels. Here’s a list of its unique strengths: Local numbers for global expansion . RingCentral lets you set up local numbers in 45 countries and territories. You can run a unified phone system for teams based across the globe. Video conferencing built into every plan . Every RingCentral plan comes with video conferencing, not just calling and texting. You can host meetings for up to 200 people, record sessions, and rely on end-to-end encryption. Desk phone rentals for teams in the office . For teams that haven’t transitioned to softphones , RingCentral still supports traditional desk phones. You can even rent hardware directly through RingCentral for an extra fee. Access to 500+ app integrations . RingCentral connects your call and text data across a library of third-party apps. For teams that want more control over their integrations, you can use its API. Multiple communication add-ons. RingCentral lets you extend communication capabilities beyond individual voice and video calls. Host group events, webinars, and hybrid conferencing with its add-ons and extensions. Multi-level IVR and call routing. RingCentral supports up to 250 auto-attendant submenus, call queues with callbacks, and ring groups. AI features. You can find AI-assisted SMS texting and summary features in RingCentral’s platform. However, you’ll also find additional usage caps here. The AI receptionist add-on, for instance, includes only 100 minutes per month before overage charges of 50 cents per minute kick in. Cons: Where RingCentral falls short Before you decide whether RingCentral is right for you, take a look at these key drawbacks: Strict texting limits . RingCentral caps outgoing texts by plan. If you exceed its limits, each extra message costs $0.0119, which adds up fast for text-heavy teams. Shared texting costs extra . Calling comes with shared numbers, but texting doesn’t. You’ll need the Business SMS Booster add-on for team-wide texting, at $25 per month. Slow texting registration . Registering your virtual number with The Campaign Registry through RingCentral can take months. Some users face repeated rejections or long stretches with no update from support. It delays their ability to text customers. Recordings expire after 90 days . RingCentral automatically deletes call recordings after 90 days. That’s a problem if you need them for training, compliance, or resolving customer issues down the line. Toll-free minutes run out quickly . RingCentral’s base plan includes just 100 toll-free minutes a month for your whole team. If you go over the limit, you’ll be charged for every additional minute you use. Outdated interface. RingCentral’s app splits calls, texts, and voicemails into separate folders. That makes it harder to follow a full customer conversation in one place. Recurring billing complaints . Users often report being billed after canceling or charged more than expected. It’s a pattern that shows up repeatedly in customer reviews. For a focused breakdown of the trade-offs, check out our analysis of RingCentral pros and cons . Is RingCentral right for your business? Now that you know where RingCentral excels and where it falls short, how do you decide if it’s right for you? Signing up for RingCentral comes down to the type of business you operate. Here’s a quick decision-making framework: Business size. If you’re a mid-market or enterprise team, RingCentral may work for you. It offers multiple channels for teams, including phone, text, video, webinars, and events. But if you’re a small team that only needs one or two channels to talk to customers, it may not be the best option. Global presence. If you have team members based outside the US and Canada, RingCentral can help them stay connected. Located in one domestic city or region? Then RingCentral may not be the most ideal fit. Feature complexity. Need advanced contact center features like multi-level IVR and workforce management tools? Then RingCentral is a good option. If you want a platform that’s easier to use and less complex, you should look elsewhere. Affordability. RingCentral offers more features through add-ons, which can cause your monthly phone costs to balloon over time. If you’re looking for a more cost-effective business phone, you should look for a RingCentral alternative. Setup speed. RingCentral can take months to get your texting registration approved. Businesses that need to text customers immediately should find a service with faster approval times. Also, if you’re a healthcare business, then you likely need a business phone that’s HIPAA compliant. Check out our article to find out if RingCentral is HIPAA compliant. How Quo compares to RingCentral If you’re looking for a RingCentral alternative for fast-growing teams, consider Quo, formerly OpenPhone. We’re the #1 rated business phone by customer satisfaction on G2. Here’s a quick look at how we’re a better alternative to RingCentral for smaller teams: Feature Quo RingCentral Starting price $15 per user per month, billed annually $20 per user per month, billed annually SMS and MMS texting to the US and Canada Unlimited texting in all plans 25–200 texts per user per month Shared texting inbox Full shared inbox, real-time visibility Requires add-on Unlimited toll-free minutes ✅ X Call recording storage limits Unlimited Determined by subscription; recordings deleted after 90 days Setup time Minutes Hours to days TCR registration 1–3 business days Can take months Integrations 9,000+ integrations available, including Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier, and Jobber 500+ integrations available, including Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, and Salesforce Claude and ChatGPT integrations ✅ X Unlimited texting and toll-free calling. Get access to all the SMS and MMS messages and toll-free minutes you need on every plan. We don’t limit teams from using essential features like calls and texts. Shared numbers for calls and texts. Share conversation context for calls and texts with your team. Shared texting is available by default in every Quo plan for local and toll-free numbers. No need to purchase any add-ons or upgrades. Smoother texting registration. Getting approved to send business texts shouldn’t take months. With Quo, you can complete US carrier registration in just 1–3 business days. We guide you through the entire process with clear steps right inside the Quo app. Plus, we offer additional US carrier registration support in our Resource Center . “After a horrible experience with RingCentral, I found my way to OpenPhone. They literally were able to overnight our TCR approval after we spent months trying to get it done through RingCentral.” – Quo user on G2 Claude and ChatGPT integrations. Share your call and text data with your favorite AI tool. Quo’s MCP integration lets you connect to both Claude and ChatGPT . Analyze call transcripts, send bulk follow-up texts, and update contact information automatically. RingCentral doesn’t have these integrations, which can slow your team down. Modern user interface. Quo has a clean and intuitive user interface that teams love to use. RingCentral’s platform is clunky and harder to navigate. It separates calls, texts, and voicemails, so your team loses context on customer conversations quickly. “Quo is extremely easy to use. We have a 6-person office routing calls to two companies, and the combination of simplicity and features is incredible. Having started with DYL (terrible system and worse service), moving to RingCentral (feature-rich but complicated and poor support), TalkRoute (great value but no features), I’ve finally found the unicorn phone system that does everything at a great price.” – Sean Williams, Managing Director, Nymble Insurance No hidden fees or surprises. With its numerous add-ons and overage charges, RingCentral pricing can feel like it has several hidden fees. Quo’s pricing keeps everything straightforward. See what you get in each plan without worrying about keeping track of your usage. See the full side-by-side comparison in our Quo vs RingCentral breakdown. Final review: Is RingCentral worth it? RingCentral is a good cloud phone system for mid-market and enterprise teams. This is especially true if they have a global presence and need multiple group communication channels. But for small and growing teams, it’s hard to recommend. With SMS and toll-free calling limits, delayed texting registration, and several add-ons, it isn’t the easiest option for small teams to use. If you’re a small team that relies on voice and text to communicate with your customers, you can find better options than RingCentral. Explore the top alternatives in our RingCentral alternatives guide. FAQs What is RingCentral? RingCentral is a cloud-based business communications platform. Founded in 1999, it’s one of the oldest platforms available in the VoIP phone market. It offers VoIP calling, texting, video conferencing, and webinars in a single platform. What is RingCentral RingEX? RingEX is RingCentral’s business phone offering. Formerly known as RingCentral MVP, RingEX provides all of RingCentral’s core business phone features. That includes calling, texting, call recording, call routing, and third-party integrations. What is RingCentral’s cancellation policy? RingCentral’s discounted pricing requires an annual contract, and plans typically auto-renew. Canceling usually means waiting until the end of your term or paying an early-termination fee. Some users report issues with billing, even after they’ve canceled their accounts: “The contract has an auto-renewal feature for an additional two years, so after two years, I was opted in by contract with no notification and stuck. Then, when the contract was over, I canceled half of my lines and was assured this was done. They continue to charge me for these lines and refuse to respond to my requests for review.” – G2 Review How does RingCentral compare to Google Voice? Google Voice is a more affordable business phone platform for teams just getting started. Pricing starts at $10 per user per month. However, it lacks business phone features like integrations, texting automations, and an AI receptionist. Google Voice suits solo users and very small teams, while RingCentral fits larger teams that need the feature depth. Check out our full Google Voice vs RingCentral comparison. How do I port my number to RingCentral? You can port an existing business number to RingCentral, but only after signing up for a paid plan. Submit a porting request with your current account number, PIN, and a recent bill. Keep your existing service active until the port completes. This typically takes a few business days to a couple of weeks, depending on the carrier.
